picks.hook_line: Is this 5, 10, 15, 20 years away? — I think it's now. I think we've achieved AGI.
picks.title: Jensen: we've already achieved AGI
picks.why: CEO of the most valuable company says AGI is here, then backs it with the claw-runs-a-viral-app scenario — instant argument-starter.

picks.hook_line: The first job AI researchers said was going to go away was radiology…
picks.title: The AI job prediction that backfired
picks.why: Complete story arc with a contrarian twist — computer vision became superhuman and radiologist jobs GREW; lands right on job-loss anxiety.
picks.note: ~102s as cut — needs a word-level trim to fit the 90s cap.

picks.hook_line: Do you think about your mortality? Are you afraid of death? — I really don't want to die.
picks.title: Jensen on death
picks.why: Rawest moment of the interview; 'this is a once-in-humanity experience' is a quotable closer.
picks.note: Composite recomputed: 2×5+3+5+5 = 23 — tied for top on voltage, docked on payoff (ends on a statement, not an arc).

picks.hook_line: The problem was CUDA increased our cost so tremendously it completely consumed all of the company's gross profit dollars.
picks.title: The bet that nearly killed Nvidia
picks.why: Market cap $8B → $1.5B, held the line anyway, 'Nvidia is the house that GeForce built' — a founding-myth story with numbers.

picks.hook_line: You think the number of programmers in the world might increase, not decrease?
picks.title: From 30 million to 1 billion coders
picks.why: 'Every carpenter will be a coder… I would completely go berserk' — concrete numbers plus an image people will repeat.

picks.hook_line: If we were to hire a new college graduate today and I have a choice between two…
picks.title: Who Jensen would hire today
picks.why: Direct career advice from Jensen — the 'expert in AI wins, whatever the job' repetition builds to 'every college student should graduate an expert in AI'.

picks.hook_line: I don't love continuous improvement — I'd rather strip it all back to zero.
picks.title: 74 days to 6 days
picks.why: Tight, self-contained first-principles lesson with a memorable number: reason from the speed of light and 74 days collapses to 6.

picks.hook_line: I actually think intelligence is a commodity.
picks.title: Intelligence is a commodity
picks.why: 'They're all superhuman to me — and somehow I'm in the middle orchestrating all 60' — humility + a provocative claim about what actually matters.

picks.hook_line: A CEO told me: Jensen, it's theoretically impossible for a fabless semiconductor company to exceed a billion dollars.
picks.title: Everyone who told Jensen 'impossible'
picks.why: Ladder of wrong predictions ($1B, $25B…) ending on 'there's nobody I could take share from' — underdog-to-untouchable arc.

picks.hook_line: On the day I say 'let's buy Mellanox', it's completely obvious to everybody that we absolutely should.
picks.title: Leading from behind
picks.why: Management insight with a name — shape belief systems daily so big decisions land as 'what took you so long?'. Below the ≥17 bar comfortably but lowest charge of the set.
picks.note: Borderline pick — included to test where the driver's quality floor is.
